title: What does ISO 45001 require for competence and awareness?
description: What ISO 45001:2018 clauses 7.2 and 7.3 require for worker competence and awareness, what auditors look for, and what the 2027 revision is expected to change.
shortAnswer: ISO 45001:2018 clause 7.2 requires an organization to determine the competence workers need for occupational health and safety performance, ensure they are competent through education, training or experience, including the ability to identify hazards, evaluate actions taken and keep evidence. Clause 7.3 requires workers to be aware of the policy, objectives, relevant hazards and incidents, and their ability to remove themselves from imminent and serious danger.
keyTakeaways: ISO 45001:2018 is the current edition, confirmed in 2024 and amended in 2024 for climate action; a revised edition is at Draft International Standard stage and expected in 2027.
Clause 7.2 goes beyond generic management system competence by requiring competence to include the ability to identify hazards.
Clause 7.2 also requires organizations to evaluate the effectiveness of competence actions and retain documented information as evidence.
Clause 7.3 lists awareness topics that include relevant incidents, hazards and risks, and the right to leave imminent and serious danger without undue consequences.
ISO 45001 is voluntary and does not replace the legal duties in the occupational health and safety legislation of any country where an organization operates.
regulator: No regulator: ISO/TC 283 maintains the standard; conformity is assessed by certification bodies
appliesTo: Organisations operating or seeking certification to an ISO 45001 OH&S management system
Workers as defined in the standard, including contractors and other people doing work under the organisation's control
Organisations integrating OH&S with ISO 9001 or ISO 14001 management systems

sections.heading: Which version of ISO 45001 applies as at September 2026?

blocks.text: ISO 45001:2018 remains the current edition. The [ISO page for ISO 45001:2018](https://www.iso.org/standard/63787.html) shows it was published in March 2018 by technical committee ISO/TC 283, was last reviewed and confirmed in 2024, and has one amendment, [ISO 45001:2018/Amd 1:2024](https://www.iso.org/standard/88428.html) on climate action changes.

A revision is well advanced. ISO lists a Draft International Standard (ISO/DIS 45001) under development and describes the next edition as planned for publication as ISO 45001:2027. [DNV](https://www.dnv.com/assurance/Management-Systems/new-iso/transition/revision-iso-45001/) reports that the DIS was released in mid June 2026 for a 12 week ballot and that publication is likely in the second half of 2027, and [SGS](https://www.sgs.com/en-sg/showcases/iso-45001-2027-key-updates-and-transition-guidance) says a three year transition period is anticipated. Until the new edition is published, certification audits are made against the 2018 edition.

ISO 45001 shares the high level structure used by ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, so clause 7 (Support) has the same layout across those standards. [ISO's overview brochure](https://www.iso.org/files/live/sites/isoorg/files/store/en/PUB100427.pdf) notes this is designed to make integration easier, and that certification is not a requirement of the standard itself. For the quality equivalent, see [ISO 9001 competence requirements](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements).

sections.heading: What does clause 7.2 require for competence?

blocks.text: Clause 7.2 requires the organization to decide what competence each worker needs for safety performance, make sure workers have it, close gaps and prove it. As publicly described by auditors and certification bodies, the clause has four parts.

items: **Determine** the necessary competence of workers that affects or can affect OH&S performance.
**Ensure** workers are competent, including the ability to identify hazards, on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience.
**Act and evaluate:** where applicable, take actions to acquire and maintain the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of those actions.
**Evidence:** retain appropriate documented information as evidence of competence.

blocks.text: Two points distinguish ISO 45001 from the generic management system text. The explicit reference to hazard identification means an auditor can reasonably ask how the organization knows a worker can recognize the hazards of their own tasks. The standard also treats training as only one route: the note to the clause gives mentoring, reassignment, and hiring or contracting competent people as other actions.

"Evaluate the effectiveness" is where many training programs fall short. A completion record shows an action was taken; it does not show the action worked. Evidence such as a practical assessment, a [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency), or supervisor observation against defined criteria is closer to what the clause asks for.

sections.heading: What does clause 7.3 require workers to be aware of?

blocks.text: Clause 7.3 requires workers to be made aware of a defined set of OH&S topics, so awareness is about specific content rather than general messaging. In summary, workers are to be made aware of:

items: the OH&S policy and OH&S objectives;
their contribution to the effectiveness of the OH&S management system, including the benefits of improved performance;
the implications and potential consequences of not conforming with the system's requirements;
incidents, and the outcomes of investigations, that are relevant to them;
hazards, OH&S risks and actions determined that are relevant to them;

their ability to remove themselves from work situations they consider present an imminent and serious danger to life or health, and the arrangements that protect them from undue consequences for doing so.

blocks.text: The last item is the most distinctive. [BSI's ISO 45001 self assessment checklist](https://www.bsigroup.com/siteassets/pdf/en/insights-and-media/insights/brochures/au-as-scert-lg-nss-hsw-iso45001-mp-occupationalhealthandsafety-0425-self-assess.pdf) frames it as all workers having the ability to remove themselves from dangerous situations and being aware of the policy protecting them from undue consequences. Where local law also gives workers a right to stop unsafe work, awareness content should explain both the organization's procedure and that legal protection.

Awareness of relevant incidents is also easy to miss. It requires a process for feeding investigation outcomes back into the information workers receive, which in turn means training content needs a trigger for review after significant incidents.

sections.heading: What evidence do auditors look for under clauses 7.2 and 7.3?

blocks.text: Auditors look for a defined competence requirement for each role, evidence that individuals meet it, and evidence that awareness topics reach workers, including contractors. The table below is an illustrative mapping from each requirement to a learning outcome and the evidence that would support it.

blocks.text: A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) is the usual tool for showing 7.2 competence requirements, and an [audit trail](/glossary/audit-trail) of content versions and assessment results supports both clauses. The steps for building the records are in [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency).

sections.heading: How does ISO 45001 relate to health and safety law?

blocks.text: ISO 45001 is a voluntary management system standard; occupational health and safety legislation is mandatory in the countries where an organization operates. Certification can help demonstrate a systematic approach, but it does not discharge the legal duty to provide the information, training, instruction and supervision the law requires.

Organizations can use one competence framework to satisfy both, provided the legal requirements for each jurisdiction are identified separately. **Example, Australia:** the model WHS Regulations require training to be suitable and adequate for the work, the risks and the controls, which maps closely to the clause 7.2 requirement to determine competence from OH&S performance needs and to include hazard identification, and section 84 of the model [Work Health and Safety Act 2011](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2011A00137/latest/text) lets a worker cease or refuse unsafe work on a reasonable concern of serious risk from an immediate or imminent exposure to a hazard, which matches the clause 7.3 awareness item on removing oneself from danger. See [the WHS Act duty to provide training](/regulations/whs-act-duty-to-provide-training).

sections.heading: What is expected to change for competence and awareness in the 2027 revision?

blocks.text: Changes to clause 7 are expected to be moderate, with the awareness list extended and more attention to reaching diverse workers. Because the DIS may still change before final publication, the points below are indicative only.

items: DNV reports that the clause 7.3 list of factors for worker awareness is extended in the draft.
SGS reports that communication should consider the diversity and needs of workers, and that information should be accessible for different roles, abilities, locations and working arrangements.
Both note wider changes elsewhere, including more emphasis on work related well being, psychosocial hazards in hazard identification, and new clauses on occupational health and return to work.

blocks.text: For training teams, the practical preparation is to confirm that competence and awareness programs reach remote, temporary and contract workers and people with different communication or accessibility needs, and that content can be updated quickly once the final text is published. Psychosocial content is covered in [psychosocial hazard training requirements](/regulations/psychosocial-hazards-training-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models clause 7.2 and 7.3 requirements as a competence framework: each role's required concepts, learning outcomes and assessment points are defined and linked to the hazards and controls they relate to. When the 2027 edition is published, the affected requirements can be updated once and the change traced to every dependent outcome. See [standards and accreditation](/platform/standards-accreditation).

faqs.q: Does ISO 45001 require formal training records for every worker?
faqs.a: Clause 7.2 requires appropriate documented information as evidence of competence. That need not be a training certificate for every task: evidence can include qualifications, licenses, assessments or documented experience. What matters is that the record shows the worker meets the competence the organization determined for the role.

faqs.q: Do contractors fall under ISO 45001 competence and awareness requirements?
faqs.a: Yes, where they are workers performing work under the organization's control. Auditors commonly check how contractor competence is verified and how contractors are made aware of site hazards, relevant incidents and the right to stop unsafe work, typically through induction and permit processes.

faqs.q: How is clause 7.3 awareness different from clause 7.4 communication?
faqs.a: Clause 7.3 defines what workers must be aware of. Clause 7.4 requires processes for internal and external communication about the OH&S management system. Communication processes are one way to achieve awareness, but awareness is judged by what workers actually know.

faqs.q: Should organizations wait for ISO 45001:2027 before updating training?
faqs.a: No. Certification is against ISO 45001:2018 until the new edition is published and transition arrangements apply. Organizations can prepare by reviewing whether training reaches all worker groups and whether content is structured so that changes in the final text can be applied quickly.

DIS stage reached mid June 2026 with a 12 week ballot; publication likely second half of 2027; clause 7.3 awareness list extended in the draft.
Three year transition anticipated; clause 7 draft changes expand awareness and require information to be accessible for different roles, abilities, locations and working arrangements.

Clause 7.2 items: determine competence; ensure competence including the ability to identify hazards on the basis of education, training or experience; take actions and evaluate effectiveness; retain documented information. Note lists training, mentoring, reassignment, hiring or contracting.
Clause 7.3 items include incidents and investigation outcomes, hazards and risks, and the ability to remove themselves from imminent and serious danger with protection from undue consequences.
BSI checklist item: all workers have the ability to remove themselves from dangerous situations and are aware of the policy protecting them from undue consequences.
ISO states ISO 45001 shares the high level structure with ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, and certification is not a requirement of the standard.
WHS Act s 84: a worker may cease or refuse work on a reasonable concern of serious risk from an immediate or imminent exposure to a hazard.
